| [High-boost filter](linear/high-boost.md) | Linear spatial filters | Sharpens by taking A times the image minus a Gaussian blur of it. | Implemented and tested |
| [High-pass filter](linear/high-pass.md) | Linear spatial filters | Keeps only the fine detail, by subtracting a Gaussian blur from the image. | Implemented and tested |
| [Laplacian](linear/laplacian.md) | Linear spatial filters | Measures how much each pixel differs from the average of its neighbors. | Implemented and tested |
| [Laplacian of Gaussian](linear/log.md) | Linear spatial filters | Smooths with a Gaussian and takes the Laplacian, the sum of the second derivatives, in one kernel. | Implemented and tested |

| [Unsharp mask](linear/unsharp-mask.md) | Linear spatial filters | Sharpens by adding back the detail that a Gaussian blur removes. | Implemented and tested |
| [Weighted average filter](linear/weighted-average.md) | Linear spatial filters | Filters with a kernel that you type, divided by its sum when you ask. | Implemented and tested |
| [Wiener filter (global)](linear/wiener-denoise.md) | Linear spatial filters | Removes white noise by turning each frequency down by how much of its power the noise explains. | Implemented and tested |
| [Adaptive median filter](nonlinear/adaptive-median.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | A median filter whose window grows where the noise is dense, and that keeps pixels that are not noise. | Implemented and tested |
| [Alpha-trimmed mean filter](nonlinear/alpha-trimmed-mean.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | Drops the smallest and largest values of each window and averages the rest. | Implemented and tested |
| [Anisotropic diffusion](nonlinear/anisotropic-diffusion.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | Smooths by letting values flow between neighbors, with a flow that stops at edges. | Implemented and tested |
| [Bilateral filter](nonlinear/bilateral.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | A blur whose weights fall with distance and with difference in value, so it smooths flat areas and stops at edges. | Implemented and tested |
| [Contraharmonic mean filter](nonlinear/contraharmonic-mean.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | A ratio of power sums with order Q. Positive Q removes pepper noise and negative Q removes salt noise. | Implemented and tested |
| [Geometric mean filter](nonlinear/geometric-mean.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | Replaces each pixel with the geometric mean of its window, the root of the product of the values. | Implemented and tested |
| [Guided filter](nonlinear/guided.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | Fits a straight-line model of the guide in every window, so it smooths flat areas and keeps edges, at a cost that does not grow with the radius. | Implemented and tested |
| [Harmonic mean filter](nonlinear/harmonic-mean.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | Replaces each pixel with the harmonic mean of its window, n divided by the sum of the inverses. | Implemented and tested |
| [Joint bilateral filter](nonlinear/joint-bilateral.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | A bilateral filter that takes its edges from a guide image, so it smooths one image along the edges of another. | Implemented and tested |
| [Kuwahara filter](nonlinear/kuwahara.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | Writes the mean of the window quadrant whose values vary the least, which smooths areas and keeps edges. | Implemented and tested |
| [Max filter](nonlinear/max.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | Replaces each pixel with the largest value of its window. | Implemented and tested |
| [Median filter](nonlinear/median.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | Replaces each pixel with the middle value of its window. | Implemented and tested |
| [Midpoint filter](nonlinear/midpoint.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | Replaces each pixel with the value halfway between the smallest and largest in its window. | Implemented and tested |
| [Min filter](nonlinear/min.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | Replaces each pixel with the smallest value of its window. | Implemented and tested |
| [Mode filter](nonlinear/mode.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | Replaces each pixel with the value that occurs most often in its window. | Implemented and tested |
| [Nagao-Matsuyama filter](nonlinear/nagao-matsuyama.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | Writes the mean of the calmest of nine subregions of a 5x5 window, with shapes that follow edges in eight directions. | Implemented and tested |
| [Rank-order filter](nonlinear/rank-order.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | Sorts each window and keeps the value at a chosen rank or percentile. | Implemented and tested |
| [Switching median filter](nonlinear/switching-median.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | Replaces a pixel by the window median only when it differs from that median by more than a threshold. | Implemented and tested |
| [Vector anisotropic diffusion](nonlinear/vector-anisotropic-diffusion.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | Anisotropic diffusion for color images, with one conduction for all channels from the color difference. | Implemented and tested |
| [Vector median filter](nonlinear/vector-median.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | Replaces each pixel with the window color that is closest, in total, to all the other window colors. | Implemented and tested |
| [Weighted median filter](nonlinear/weighted-median.md) | Nonlinear spatial filters | A median in which each window position counts as many times as its weight. | Implemented and tested |
| [Adaptive Wiener filter](adaptive/wiener-adaptive.md) | Adaptive and statistical filters | Moves each pixel toward its local mean by an amount set by how the local variance compares with the noise variance. | Implemented and tested |
| [Adaptive local noise reduction](adaptive/adaptive-local-noise.md) | Adaptive and statistical filters | Subtracts a share of the difference between each pixel and its local mean, set by the noise variance over the local variance. | Implemented and tested |
| [Adaptive smoothing](adaptive/adaptive-smoothing.md) | Adaptive and statistical filters | Repeats a 3x3 weighted mean in which pixels with a large gradient get little weight, so edges are not smoothed across. | Implemented and tested |
| [Enhanced Lee filter](adaptive/enhanced-lee.md) | Adaptive and statistical filters | A Lee filter with three classes. Flat areas get the mean, strong targets stay unchanged, and areas between are blended. | Implemented and tested |
| [Entropy filter](adaptive/local-entropy.md) | Adaptive and statistical filters | Maps the entropy of the values in the window around each pixel, a measure of how varied they are. | Implemented and tested |
| [Frost filter](adaptive/frost.md) | Adaptive and statistical filters | A weighted mean whose weights fall exponentially with distance, faster where the local variation is high. | Implemented and tested |
| [Gamma-MAP filter](adaptive/gamma-map.md) | Adaptive and statistical filters | The maximum a posteriori estimate for gamma-distributed scene and speckle, with the classes of the enhanced Lee filter. | Implemented and tested |
| [Kuan filter](adaptive/kuan.md) | Adaptive and statistical filters | A speckle filter like the Lee filter, with a weight derived without the approximation Lee made. | Implemented and tested |
| [Lee filter](adaptive/lee.md) | Adaptive and statistical filters | Moves each pixel toward its local mean by a share set by how its local variation compares with the speckle variation. | Implemented and tested |
| [Local variance filter](adaptive/local-variance.md) | Adaptive and statistical filters | Maps the variance of the window around each pixel, a measure of local contrast and texture. | Implemented and tested |
| [Median absolute deviation thresholding](adaptive/mad-outlier.md) | Adaptive and statistical filters | Marks or repairs values that lie more than t times the robust scale S from the local median. | Implemented and tested |
| [Range filter](adaptive/local-range.md) | Adaptive and statistical filters | Maps the difference between the largest and smallest value in the window around each pixel. | Implemented and tested |
| [Savitzky-Golay filter](adaptive/savgol.md) | Adaptive and statistical filters | Fits a polynomial to each window by least squares and takes its value at the center, a smoothing that keeps peaks. | Implemented and tested |
| [Sigma filter](adaptive/sigma.md) | Adaptive and statistical filters | Averages only the window values that lie within k sigma of the center value, and repairs isolated spots. | Implemented and tested |
| [Speckle reducing anisotropic diffusion](adaptive/srad.md) | Adaptive and statistical filters | Diffusion whose coefficient comes from the local coefficient of variation, so speckle diffuses away and edges stay. | Implemented and tested |
| [Standard deviation filter](adaptive/local-std.md) | Adaptive and statistical filters | Maps the standard deviation of the window around each pixel, a measure of local contrast in levels. | Implemented and tested |
| [Alternating sequential filter](morphology/asf.md) | Morphological filters | Openings and closings with elements of growing size, one pair per size. It removes bright and dark details up to a size, step by step. | Implemented and tested |
| [Black-hat](morphology/blackhat.md) | Morphological filters | The closing minus the image. It keeps dark details smaller than the element. | Implemented and tested |
| [Closing](morphology/closing.md) | Morphological filters | Dilation followed by erosion. It fills dark details smaller than the element and keeps the rest. | Implemented and tested |
| [Closing by reconstruction](morphology/closing-by-reconstruction.md) | Morphological filters | A dilation followed by reconstruction by erosion. It fills dark objects the element does not fit into and restores the others exactly. | Implemented and tested |
| [Connected-component filtering](morphology/ccl-filter.md) | Morphological filters | Keeps the white objects whose area lies in a range and removes the others. | Implemented and tested |
| [Convex hull](morphology/convex-hull.md) | Morphological filters | Replaces every white object with its convex hull, the smallest convex shape that contains it. | Implemented and tested |
| [Dilation](morphology/dilation.md) | Morphological filters | Takes the largest value under the turned structuring element, so bright objects grow and dark details shrink. | Implemented and tested |
| [Erosion](morphology/erosion.md) | Morphological filters | Takes the smallest value under the structuring element, so dark areas grow and bright objects shrink. | Implemented and tested |
| [External gradient](morphology/external-gradient.md) | Morphological filters | The dilation minus the image. It marks the outer side of bright edges. | Implemented and tested |
| [Geodesic filtering](morphology/geodesic.md) | Morphological filters | A fixed number of geodesic dilation or erosion steps. The marker grows under the image, or shrinks over it, one pixel per step. | Implemented and tested |
| [Hit-or-miss transform](morphology/hit-or-miss.md) | Morphological filters | Marks the pixels where a small pattern of foreground and background pixels matches exactly. | Implemented and tested |
| [Internal gradient](morphology/internal-gradient.md) | Morphological filters | The image minus its erosion. It marks the inner side of bright edges. | Implemented and tested |
| [Morphological gradient](morphology/morph-gradient.md) | Morphological filters | Dilation minus erosion. It is bright on edges, with a width set by the element. | Implemented and tested |
| [Morphological leveling](morphology/leveling.md) | Morphological filters | Moves the image toward a marker, such as a blurred copy, while keeping every edge sharp. Flat zones grow and merge, but their borders never move. | Implemented and tested |
| [Morphological reconstruction](morphology/reconstruction.md) | Morphological filters | Grows a marker under the image until it stops, which restores every bright region the marker touches and flattens the rest. | Implemented and tested |
| [Opening](morphology/opening.md) | Morphological filters | Erosion followed by dilation. It removes bright details smaller than the element and keeps the rest. | Implemented and tested |
| [Opening by reconstruction](morphology/opening-by-reconstruction.md) | Morphological filters | An erosion followed by reconstruction by dilation. It removes bright objects the element does not fit into and restores the others exactly. | Implemented and tested |
| [Pruning](morphology/pruning.md) | Morphological filters | Removes short branches, or spurs, from thinned lines while keeping the main lines at their full length. | Implemented and tested |

| [Thinning](morphology/thinning.md) | Morphological filters | Removes boundary pixels of white shapes until lines one pixel thick remain, without breaking or joining shapes. | Implemented and tested |
| [Top-hat](morphology/tophat.md) | Morphological filters | The image minus its opening. It keeps bright details smaller than the element and removes the background. | Implemented and tested |
| [Butterworth band-pass](frequency/butterworth-bandpass.md) | Frequency-domain filters | Keeps only a ring of frequencies, which leaves the detail of one size. The cutoff is smooth, and the order sets how sharp it is. | Implemented and tested |

| [Gaussian band-pass](frequency/gaussian-bandpass.md) | Frequency-domain filters | Keeps only a ring of frequencies, which leaves the detail of one size. The band edges follow a Gaussian curve, so they ring very little. | Implemented and tested |
| [Gaussian band-reject](frequency/gaussian-bandreject.md) | Frequency-domain filters | Removes a ring of frequencies and keeps the rest, which suppresses noise or patterns of one size. The band edges follow a Gaussian curve, so they ring very little. | Implemented and tested |
| [Gaussian high-pass](frequency/gaussian-highpass.md) | Frequency-domain filters | Removes the low frequencies of the image and keeps the high ones, which leaves edges and fine detail. The cutoff follows a Gaussian curve, so it does not ring. | Implemented and tested |
| [Gaussian low-pass](frequency/gaussian-lowpass.md) | Frequency-domain filters | Keeps the low frequencies of the image and removes the high ones, which blurs it. The cutoff follows a Gaussian curve, so it does not ring. | Implemented and tested |

| [Ideal band-pass](frequency/ideal-bandpass.md) | Frequency-domain filters | Keeps only a ring of frequencies, which leaves the detail of one size. The cutoff is sharp. | Implemented and tested |
| [Ideal band-reject](frequency/ideal-bandreject.md) | Frequency-domain filters | Removes a ring of frequencies and keeps the rest, which suppresses noise or patterns of one size. The cutoff is sharp. | Implemented and tested |
| [Ideal high-pass](frequency/ideal-highpass.md) | Frequency-domain filters | Removes the low frequencies of the image and keeps the high ones, which leaves edges and fine detail. The cutoff is sharp. | Implemented and tested |
| [Ideal low-pass](frequency/ideal-lowpass.md) | Frequency-domain filters | Keeps the low frequencies of the image and removes the high ones, which blurs it. The cutoff is sharp. | Implemented and tested |
| [Log-Gabor filter](frequency/log-gabor.md) | Frequency-domain filters | A band-pass filter that is a Gaussian on a log frequency scale, so it has no response at frequency 0 and a long tail toward fine detail. | Implemented and tested |
